Critical Thinking Cases and Questions
Case Study 1
A 50-year-old man complains of burning and diffuse pain in his 
left ear over a period of 2 days. Today, he noted rash breaking out 
in the posterior part of the left external ear and mastoid region. On 
examination, there is a red rash with blisters starting on his back 
part of left ear and involving posteriorly on mastoid region. Some 
motor weakness of left facial region was also observed. See Chapter 
38 “Facial Nerve and its Disorders”.

selected_evidence.unit_text:
Sensory epithelial hair cells (Fig. 25): The sensory hair 
cells are of two types: type 1 and type 2. From the 
upper surface of each cell projects a kinocilium and 
multiple stereocilia. The kinocilium, which is thicker than 
stereocilia, is located on the edge of the cell. Sensory 
cells are surrounded by supporting cells which have 
microvilli on their upper surface. Hair cells of both types 
may have contact with the same nerve calyx.

The middle ear cleft (Fig. 8), which is lined by mucous membrane 
and filled with air, consists of the middle ear, Eustachian tube, 
aditus ad antrum, mastoid antrum and mastoid air cells. Middle 
ear is a 1–2 cm3 air-filled cavity that houses ossicles (malleus,

(chorda tympani, tympanic plexus).

selected_evidence.unit_text:
The pinna collects sound signal1 from the environment, 
which passes through EAC and vibrates the TM (Fig. 29). 
Vibrations of the TM are transmitted to the stapes footplate 
through the chain of ossicles.2 Vibrations of stapes footplate 
result in the pressure changes in the labyrinthine fluids3 

that lead to movement of the basilar membrane and thus 
stimulate the hair cells of the organ of Corti. The IHC of cochlea 
act as transducers and convert the mechanical energy into 
electrical impulses which travel along the auditory nerve.

selected_evidence.unit_text:
The pinna collects sound signal1 from the environment, 
which passes through EAC and vibrates the TM (Fig. 29). 
Vibrations of the TM are transmitted to the stapes footplate 
through the chain of ossicles.2 Vibrations of stapes footplate 
result in the pressure changes in the labyrinthine fluids3 

that lead to movement of the basilar membrane and thus 
stimulate the hair cells of the organ of Corti. The IHC of cochlea 
act as transducers and convert the mechanical energy into 
electrical impulses which travel along the auditory nerve.
